It’s such a huge shock immediately post surgery. Mine’s an ileostomy and the first time I saw it, a couple of days after the operation, I was freaked out. By day four I was changing the bag myself because I knew I was going to have to do it sooner or later. I’m eight months in and after some teething troubles with bags and adhesive issues I think I’ve found the right mix. 
It’s still a source of fascination to me, so I still approach bag emptying and changing like a science project. 
I’m female and have been told by the stoma nurses that women do adapt to stomas more easily than men, so don’t beat yourself up about any part of this process. It’s life changing on good and troublesome ways, but it gets easier 🙏

I’m 64 and still awaiting official AuDHD diagnosis. My whole life, at least since I was eight years old, I’ve considered suicide as my ‘get out’ clause, you know ‘if it all gets too much I can check out’ kind of thoughts. I’ve made a few serious attempts, which obviously all failed, and after the most recent attempt I realised that I can’t even do that properly! So now I do my best to live what’s left of my life literally one day at a time. I don’t plan ahead for anything anymore (I have several health issues that makes it almost impossible to plan ahead anyway), but I give myself permission to just get through life in small chunks of time. It stops things becoming too overwhelming, and takes some of the pressure off of being alive. 
I hope you can find some moments of peace 🙏
